title: Following an adult's gaze rose gradually after 6 months in one lab study
summary: In a monthly lab study of 43 infants, gaze-following and point-following did not beat chance until after 6 months, then rose slowly through 12 months.
body: Tang, Gonzalez, and Deak tested 43 North American middle-class infants every month from 4 to 12 months. The babies learned that a correct location would play a reward video. Following an adult's gaze, a point, or both increased gradually from about 7 months. It did not exceed chance until after 6 months. A separate group tested only at 9 and 12 months suggested the rise was not just practice from monthly visits. Infants rarely followed a cue to a location behind them, even at 12 months. The authors limit the result to this controlled setting and this sample. The licence of the article is CC BY-NC-ND, so this card paraphrases and does not quote.

sources.title: The slow emergence of gaze- and point-following
sources.author: Yueyan Tang, Marybel Robledo Gonzalez, and Gedeon O. Deak
sources.note: Supports the N=43 monthly result: no above-chance following until after 6 months, gradual rise from about 7 months, and rare following to locations behind the infant. Paraphrase only (CC BY-NC-ND).
